briefs.name: MGM Resorts International
briefs.about: MGM Resorts runs casinos and hotels, including the Bellagio and MGM Grand in Las Vegas. It also has casinos in Macau, China, and co-owns BetMGM, an online sports betting app.
briefs.whyMoved: MGM fell 3.37% in the week of November 16 to 20, from a $33.61 Monday open to a $32.36 Friday close, the low of the day, with Friday's 5.8 million shares the busiest of the week. That was still far better than the S&P 500's 8.6% drop that week, because casinos do not depend on the AI spending that crashed tech stocks. The Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix ran through the Strip from November 19 to 21, with MGM partners like Pepsi running free food stops next to Park MGM, but no report yet shows how much extra money race week brought in. MGM makes most of its money from Las Vegas hotel rooms and casinos, so its stock moves on signs of how many visitors come and how much they spend.

watch.what: MGM's fourth-quarter report after the close. Beating about $0.50 profit per share and $4.42 billion of sales would be good; Las Vegas room sales falling again would be bad.

briefs.name: Dow
briefs.headline: Dow gains 423 points and closes back above 50,000 as shoppers feel better
briefs.summary: The Conference Board's consumer confidence score rose 11.4 points to 103.3, the highest since January 2025, and 30.8% of people said jobs are 'plentiful', up from 26.2%. Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $41 billion in cash. Health care stocks were the strongest group early in the day, up about 2.1%. On Monday the Dow jumped about 3% as Nvidia rose 31.5% when Jensen Huang returned as CEO.
bull: Consumer confidence hit 103.3 on Nov 24, the best since January 2025, which is good for Dow shopping names like Walmart and Nike before the holidays.
Health care members rose on Nov 24, with Johnson & Johnson and Merck up 2% to 4% and UnitedHealth about 3%, showing money moving into steadier companies.
Because only a few of its 30 companies make chips, the Dow rose 0.85% on a day the chip index fell nearly 8%.
bear: Traders see about a 95% chance the Fed raises rates on Dec 9, which raises borrowing costs for big companies and their customers.
Shoppers still expect prices to rise 5.7% over the next 12 months, per the Nov 24 survey, and high inflation could make the Fed raise rates more.
Member Nvidia fell about 6% on Nov 24 after its 31.5% jump on Monday, showing how quickly the AI rally can wobble.

briefs.about: The Dow Jones Industrial Average tracks 30 big, well-known US companies, like Apple, Walmart, Nike, Johnson & Johnson and Nvidia. It is the oldest major US stock index.
briefs.whyMoved: The Dow rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, on Tuesday, November 24, to 50,018.70, closing back above 50,000 after slipping below that mark on November 19 for the first time since June. It rose while the Nasdaq fell 1.48% because most of its 30 companies are not chip makers: Nike jumped nearly 6%, Walmart, Johnson & Johnson and Merck rose 2% to 4%, UnitedHealth about 3%, and Apple and Microsoft about 1%. Member Nvidia fell about 6%, but the Dow is weighted by share price, so pricier stocks like UnitedHealth move it more. Good news for shoppers helped, as November consumer confidence jumped to 103.3.

watch.what: October PCE inflation, the Fed's favorite price gauge, and a second look at summer growth (GDP) at 8:30 a.m. Eastern; core PCE is expected at 3.2% over a year, so a lower number would ease rate-hike worries and a higher one would add to them.
US stock markets are closed for Thanksgiving, and on Friday, Nov 27, they close early at 1 p.m. Eastern, so trading will be light.
Fed rate decision: traders put about 95% odds on a quarter-point hike to 4.00%-4.25%; a bigger hike or talk of more hikes would likely hurt, while a calmer message could help.

briefs.name: Russell 2000
briefs.headline: Russell 2000 rises 0.6% as money moves from chip giants to smaller companies
briefs.summary: On November 18, Russell 2000 futures (contracts that bet on the index) fell to 2,694.40, their lowest since April 13, then bounced after the Fed's meeting notes matched what traders expected. Strong reports from TJX and Target that week showed shoppers still spending before Black Friday. In the Nov 24 survey, 30.8% of people said jobs are 'plentiful', up from 26.2%. Shoppers still expect prices to rise 5.7% over the next year.
bull: Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 on Nov 24, the best since January 2025, which matters because most small companies sell mainly to US shoppers.
Retailers are beating forecasts: Best Buy's same-store sales rose 6.1% and Dick's and Dollar Tree raised their outlooks on Nov 24.
Worries about AI spending are pushing some money from tech giants to smaller firms, as Nov 24 showed when the Russell rose while a chip index fell nearly 8%.
bear: Traders see about a 95% chance of a Fed rate hike on Dec 9; many small companies have loans whose rates rise with the Fed's, so their interest bills go up fast.
Russell 2000 futures hit their lowest level since April 13 on Nov 18, showing how weak smaller companies have been this month.
Shoppers expect 5.7% inflation over the next year, and if prices keep rising they may spend less at the stores many small companies run.

briefs.about: The Russell 2000 tracks about 2,000 smaller US companies, like regional banks, factories and store chains. Most of them sell mainly inside the US, so it shows how the US economy itself is doing.
briefs.whyMoved: The Russell 2000 rose 15.29 points, or 0.57%, on Tuesday, November 24, to 2,684.94, while the Nasdaq fell 1.48%. Investors sold big chip stocks after Monday's Nvidia rally and moved some money into companies that depend on US shoppers, and few small companies make AI chips. A jump in consumer confidence to 103.3, the highest since January 2025, helped, because most Russell companies sell at home. Store chains reporting strong results also lifted the mood: Dick's Sporting Goods jumped about 15%, Dollar Tree about 11% and Best Buy about 5%.

watch.what: October PCE inflation, the Fed's favorite price gauge, and a second look at summer growth (GDP) at 8:30 a.m. Eastern; core PCE is expected at 3.2% over a year, so a lower number would ease rate-hike worries and a higher one would add to them.
Black Friday, the biggest shopping day of the year; strong sales would help small US store chains, while weak sales would hint shoppers are pulling back.
Fed rate decision: traders put about 95% odds on a quarter-point hike to 4.00%-4.25%; a bigger hike or talk of more hikes would likely hurt, while a calmer message could help.

briefs.headline: Micron drops 11% to $629.79, giving back most of Monday's 19% jump
briefs.about: Micron makes memory chips, the parts that store data in computers, phones and the giant data centers that run AI. Its main products are DRAM and NAND flash memory, plus HBM, a fast memory built for AI chips.
briefs.summary: Micron is now 48% below its June 25 high of $1,213.56 and down 32% in the past month, which counts as a bear market (a fall of 20% or more). About 38.9 million shares traded Tuesday, above the 20-day average of about 35.9 million, so many owners were selling at once. Even after the drop, the stock is still up about 131% this year, 24/7 Wall St. noted. Bloomingbit reported a US Senate hearing set for December 3 tied to the Nvidia questions.
bull: Micron's last quarter (reported September 30) brought in $54.23 billion in sales, up 379% from a year earlier, so demand for its chips has been huge.
Micron forecast next quarter's sales at about $61.5 billion, higher than last quarter, which shows it expects AI memory demand to keep growing.
The stock is still about 180% above its low of $224.53 from November 2025, so long-time owners are still far ahead.
bear: The 11% drop on Nov 24 wiped out most of Monday's gain in one day, showing how fast Micron swings with news about Nvidia.
A US Senate hearing on December 3 and a board investigation into Nvidia's CEO could keep worries about AI spending alive.
Micron is down 32% in a month and 48% from its June high, a sign many investors fear memory prices have peaked.

briefs.name: Micron Technology
briefs.whyMoved: Micron fell $77.91, or 11%, on Tuesday, November 24, from $707.70 to $629.79, giving back about 69% of Monday's 19% jump. The whole chip group sank: a chip index fell 7.9%, Nvidia dropped 5.9% a day after jumping 31.5%, and fellow memory makers SanDisk fell 11.1% and Western Digital 7.8%. Reports named profit-taking after Monday's rally, worries about higher tariffs, a board investigation into Nvidia's Jensen Huang and unconfirmed reports of a government probe into Nvidia. That matters for Micron because Nvidia is one of the biggest buyers of the HBM memory Micron sells for AI chips, and Micron earns most of its money when AI data centers keep buying memory at high prices.

watch.what: US Senate hearing tied to Nvidia. Calm news could help chip stocks; new problems for Nvidia could pull Micron lower again.
Fed rate decision. Traders see about a 95% chance of a rate hike; signs of more hikes would hurt fast-moving chip stocks like Micron.
Micron's quarterly report. Watch whether sales reach about $61.5 billion, its own forecast; a miss or weaker memory prices would be a bad sign.

briefs.headline: Domino's gets an upgrade to a $400 target, but US store sales grew just 0.3%
briefs.about: Domino's Pizza is the world's biggest pizza delivery chain. Most of its stores are run by franchise owners, who pay Domino's fees and buy dough, cheese and other supplies from it.
briefs.whyMoved: Domino's rose about 2.5% on the morning of November 13 after the research firm Baird upgraded it to 'outperform' and raised its target to $400 from $320, about 20% above the prior day's close. Baird sees a 'clearer path' to better sales because the average order size grew in the third quarter and Domino's is shortening its discount deals and adding menu items people add on. The rest of the two weeks was quiet, and the stock is still down more than 18% in 2026. Domino's makes most of its money from fees franchise owners pay on their sales and from selling them supplies, so its profit depends on sales at existing stores, which grew only 0.3% in the US last quarter.
briefs.summary: Third-quarter revenue was $1.19 billion and profit was $4.60 a share, both above what analysts expected. Global retail sales rose 3.2% to $4.84 billion, slower than 6.3% a year earlier, and international same-store sales rose just 0.2%. On October 30 Domino's lowered its 2026 goal for new US stores and for operating profit growth, citing pressure on franchise owners' profits. BMO Capital also rates Domino's 'outperform' with a $390 target, while 16 of 30 analysts say hold.
bull: Baird's November 13 upgrade to a $400 target points to bigger average orders, which matter because more money per order helps both Domino's and its franchise owners.
Profit per share rose to $4.60 from $4.08 a year earlier, even though US store sales barely grew.
13 of 30 analysts rate Domino's a buy and only 1 says sell, with targets as high as $425.
bear: US same-store sales grew only 0.3% last quarter, down from 5.2% a year earlier, and the CFO expects 2026 growth at the low end of low single digits.
Domino's cut its 2026 goal for new US stores on October 30, and Baird warns weaker 2026 results will likely slow store openings in 2027 too.
Markets expect a Fed rate hike at the December 8-9 meeting, and higher rates make it costlier for franchise owners to borrow money to open stores.

watch.what: Fed rate decision. A hike is expected; more hikes would raise franchise owners' borrowing costs and could slow new store openings.
